the date of the first check in January

blocks: The left column is the work of Justice, which stands in the minus of the month. In 2028 Justice will take the centre of the year’s matrix, and December is the last moment to enter the year of Justice without loose ends. The right column is the work of the Fool in the plus of the month.

formula.caption: **22 → 22.** The Fool from the upper point of December will stand in the left point of the 2028 matrix, which is read for how to behave with people. The last month of the year already speaks in the voice of the next.

blocks: The Fool, familiar from February and June, stands in the pure plus in December, and in 2028 it will stand where you can see what people expect of you. December lets you try it in advance: lightness and readiness for the new. A plan written on a wave of the Chariot and the Fool comes out bolder than usual, and room for the unexpected has to be left in it deliberately.

The people point of December is the Empress: care, generosity, home, celebration. Those around you ask for warmth in a broad sense — attention, a gift, time. In October the Empress stood in the weak spot and warned of excess; in December it faces people, and generosity towards them balances the end-of-year rush well. The weak spot is the Hierophant, your centre. Many people know the December version: a family celebration where you explain to everyone how to live properly. Your rules are good for you; at the festive table it is better to keep them to yourself unless asked.

**What to put off in December.** New commitments for next year taken on in the pre-holiday rush. Towards the end of the year it is easy to promise a lot; it is better to enter 2028 with what you calmly chose in your plan.

Below, in the corners of the month, are the Moon, your trigger, and Strength, the centre of the year. Anxiety before the New Year likes to pass itself off as a premonition, and Strength next to it suggests what to do with it: hold the pause until it becomes clear whether it is a fact or a fear. The sum of all December’s points is 10, the Wheel: the arcanum that stood in the minus all year becomes the hint of the month in December. Count how many times during the year you caught a moment you had prepared for. That is the answer to the main money question of 2027.
actions: By 20 December, close everything that can be closed: debts, signatures, returns, promises.
Write a plan for 2028 on one page: three goals, the first step of each, an empty slot for the unexpected.
Give your loved ones time and attention — the Empress stands in the people point.
At the festive table, share your rules only if asked about them.

chapters.conclusion: In relationships 2027 values calm strength: you want to be with a person you don’t have to compete with, and you yourself grow when you stop winning arguments. The plus of the year is alliance and personal space, the minus is a repeat of old scenarios, the weak spot is a wish to blow everything up. From April the age ring holds the Lovers: the second half of the year is a time of choice in closeness.

cards.label: Plus of the year and your ring from April
cards.caption: The Lovers in the upper point of the year and on the age ring from 7 April 2027: alliance, choice, partnership.

blocks: For a forecast of personal life Lisovskaya advises starting with the relationship line, then looking at the karmic tail, and then at the age ring. The year’s matrix is then read in special meanings: the points “slightly change their sense”. The upper point and the upper left corner show the plus of personal life — what to expect, how to support the relationship, what inspires. The right and lower points show trials and mistakes. The upper right corner shows weak spots and secret desires that lead the wrong way. The left point shows how to tune the relationship, through what and where, which qualities to look for in another person. The centre is the true desire of the period. The lower corners are intuitive impulses in behaviour with a loved one.

formula.caption: **12 → 19 → 7.** Your relationship line matches your karmic tail. Closeness is where the tail is most noticeable, and in the year of Strength this is felt especially.

blocks.h3: Your relationship line and the tail

blocks: Your relationship line runs from the Hanged Man through the Sun to the Chariot, and this trio also forms your karmic tail. At the entrance is the Hanged Man: in relationships you look for a chance to see yourself differently, and if so, you may also put up with things longer than you should. Making up with you is easiest through the Sun — warmth, simplicity, an open conversation without subtext. The dual, a person who is “your own” by energy, is the Chariot: mobile, active, with a road of their own. Lisovskaya describes a tail with these numbers as the task of learning to hear the other side and settle conflicts with words. In 2027 this task coincides with the centre of the year.

blocks.h3: The year’s matrix in the meanings of love

blocks: **True desire — 11 Strength.** The centre of the year in the love reading is what is truly valuable to you in a close person during this period. Strength here is the wish to be with someone you don’t have to compete with and don’t have to win over every day: with a person who has a calm strength of their own. And the wish to be strong yourself without pressure — so that being next to you feels reliable, not cramped.

**How to tune the relationship — 21 the World.** The left point suggests through what and where to build closeness, which qualities to look at. The World — through breadth: trips together, new places, shared projects that go beyond everyday life. The qualities worth paying attention to are freedom, a broad outlook, the ability to finish what was started, ease in dealing with different people. The mistake of this point is to dissolve the relationship in endless plans and give it no footing.

**Plus — 6 the Lovers and 9 the Hermit.** In 2027 relationships grow through choice and alliance and at the same time through personal space. The Lovers mean shared decisions, agreements, renewal of feelings, co-creation. The Hermit means time alone with yourself and deep conversations for two. A couple in which each has their own silence is stronger this year than a couple that is together all the time.

**Minus — 10 the Wheel twice.** The trials of the year in love are repetition. An old quarrel scenario plays out a second time, a person from the past reappears, a decision in a burst of emotion — to break up or, on the contrary, to urgently get everything back — triggers a long chain of consequences. If you recognise a familiar turn, it is a signal to stop and take at least one step differently from last time.

**Weak spot — 16 the Tower.** A secret desire that leads the wrong way: to blow everything up when bored or hurt, “all or nothing”. According to the book this point shows minuses that hit not the partner but you yourself. An abrupt break-up in the heat of the moment is exactly such a minus. Especially until April, while the Tower also stands on the ring.

**Intuitive impulses — 20 Judgement and 4 the Emperor.** Judgement pulls you to review the past, talk about family and lineage, evaluate — yourself, your partner, the relationship. The Emperor pulls you to protect, take responsibility, build a home and order. Both impulses are good as long as they don’t turn into judging your partner and controlling them.

blocks.h3: The typical quarrel of 2027 and the way out of it

blocks: If you put the points of the year together with your relationship line, the year has a recognisable quarrel scenario. It starts with a sense of unfairness: someone close said or did something that seems unfair — Justice, the hint of the year, makes you especially sensitive to this, and Judgement in the lower corner pulls you to pass judgement at once. Then your speed switches on: the answer comes faster than you have managed to cool down. After a few exchanges the argument goes into “all or nothing” — that is the Tower in the weak spot. And then, a week or a month later, everything repeats almost word for word — that is the Wheel in the minus.

The way out can also be read from the chart. The first step is Strength: stop at the moment you want to answer back and say “I’ll come back to this conversation in the evening.” The second is the Hanged Man at the entrance to your relationship line: look at the situation through the other’s eyes and ask yourself what they really meant. The third is the Sun, the point through which it is easiest to make up with you: return to the conversation simply and warmly, without a long analysis of who was right. A short “this hurt me, and I don’t want it to drive us apart” works better this year than an hour-long discussion.

blocks.h3: If you are in a couple

blocks: The first third of the year is a time to look honestly at the relationship and break nothing in the heat of the moment. Spring and summer are a time to renew the alliance: a shared project, a trip for two, an agreement about how you live now — the Lovers in the centre of May and in the plus of July support such steps. Autumn is the time of the choice that the whole third third led up to. It can be different: deepen the alliance, make it official, agree on new rules or admit that your paths are parting. The matrix doesn’t make this choice; it shows that it works best from a calm place, without a quarrel, and that November is the hardest month for a decision.

blocks.h3: If you are single

blocks: From April, when the ring moves to the Lovers, the year shows a clear interest in new acquaintances. The World in the left point suggests where they are more likely: on trips, in study, in new groups of people, among people from another circle or from other places. The main risk is the Wheel in the minus: going back to a former partner because it is familiar, or choosing someone with whom an old story repeats. A useful question with each new acquaintance: does this person resemble my past or what I want now?

blocks: In 2027 the Lovers move from place to place, and they show when the theme of closeness comes to the fore and in what form.

blocks.h3: Loved ones, parents, friends

blocks: Judgement in the lower right corner of the year and in the result of the first third makes 2027 a time for conversations with family. February, with the Hanged Man in the centre, touches your parents’ point; July, with the Hierophant, touches family get-togethers and celebrations. If there is a conversation in the family that has long been put off, the year has two good windows for it: February and July.
actions: Agree with someone close on one rule for arguments for the year, for example: a difficult conversation only when both have cooled down.
Plan one trip or shared project for two for May–July.
If you are single, from April choose settings where you meet people from another circle: trips, courses, new groups.
When you recognise a familiar turn of an old scenario in a relationship, name it out loud and take one step differently from last time.
Use February or July for the family conversation that has long been put off.

chapters.conclusion: In money, 2027 supports partnerships, contracts and concentrating on one undertaking, and puts the main risk in repetition: impulsive decisions, debts, betting on luck. The year hits three points of your money set-up — your material task, your point of profit and your entrance to money: it is good for harvesting earlier investments and bad for leaping after fast money.

cards.label: Material point of the year — and of every month
cards.caption: The Wheel in the right point of the year also stands in the right point of all twelve monthly matrices — that is how the calculation works. The risk of repetition and impulse accompanies the whole year.

blocks: Lisovskaya builds a forecast for finances and work in a set order: first the person’s money line, then the material karma, then the age ring. The year’s matrix is then read in special meanings shared by love and money: the upper point and upper left corner are the plus, the right and lower points are trials and mistakes, the upper right corner is weak spots and secret desires, the left point is how to tune your affairs, the centre is the true desire, the lower corners are intuitive impulses.

formula.caption: **8 → 21 → 13.** Your material karma. The middle point is the sum of the two outer ones: 8 + 13 = 21.

blocks.h3: Your money set-up

blocks: According to Lisovskaya, material karma is a line a person passes in the minus from birth, and its task is to bring these energies into the plus. Your main point is 8, Justice: the theme of honesty, law, calculation in material matters, and in the minus — judging people instead of understanding them, and harshness. The middle one is 21, the World, the attitude to the material: freedom and breadth, and in the minus — irresponsibility and a feeling that circumstances are stronger than you. The entrance to money is 13, Death, in the book’s words “an entrance and a block at the same time”: money comes through renewal and closes off when a person clings to what has outlived itself.

Your money line runs from the entrance through Judgement, the point of profit, to the Chariot at the crossing of money and relationships: 13 → 20 → 7. According to Lisovskaya, the point of profit shows where the biggest earnings come from. The Chariot at the end of the line in the money sense means attitudes that get in the way of earning, and at the same time the dual, a person who can influence your earnings either way.

blocks.h3: Where the year touches this set-up

blocks: Three matches belong specifically to 2027. The hint of the year is 8, the main point of your material karma. The corner “what the year is good for” is 20, your point of profit; Judgement also sums up the first third and stands in the plus of October. The centre of September is 13, your entrance to money. The year passes through the beginning and end of your material karma and through the middle of your money line. This is neither a promise of money nor a threat: material decisions in 2027 will be more noticeable than usual, and working with your material karma — an honest count, renewal, freedom without irresponsibility — will give more than usual.

There is also a constant note worth telling apart from a sign of the year. The left point of any non-leap year of yours is 21, and it matches the “attitude to the material”. It was so in 2026 and will be so in 2029. This is the background of your ordinary years: the world around you keeps asking how freely and responsibly you handle money and things.

blocks.h3: The year’s matrix in the meanings of money

blocks: **True desire — 11 Strength.** In money and work the centre of the year is the wish to run your own work yourself: to organise, lead, hold the process in your hands. If you are employed without subordinates, this wish is there too, it just looks different: an area you are fully responsible for and the right to make decisions in it. The minus of Strength in money is working yourself into the ground for a result, when burnout eats up what you earned.

**How to tune your affairs — 21 the World.** Through breadth: remote projects, clients and partners from other cities and countries, new markets, languages. It is worth looking at terms that leave you freedom and at obligations you will really fulfil.

**Plus — 6 the Lovers and 9 the Hermit.** Partnership, contracts, support from outside — and at the same time remote work, concentration on one undertaking, self-sufficiency. It looks as if the best money format of the year is an alliance of two independent people: each does their own thing, and together it sells better.

**Minus — 10 the Wheel twice.** Debts and loans, impulsive decisions, trusting the wrong person, the return of old debts and schemes. This is the main money point of the year. The plus of the Wheel — opportunities, a big payout, debts being repaid — is there too, and goes to whoever was prepared.

**Weak spot — 16 the Tower.** A secret wish to change everything at once: quit your job without a plan, put everything into one idea, buy in the heat of the moment. Rebuilding in money is good in June, when the Tower is in the plus, and according to a plan.

**Intuitive impulses — 20 Judgement and 4 the Emperor.** Judgement pulls towards expansion and searching for a new occupation, the Emperor towards ambition, promotion, a business of your own, stability. These impulses are worth listening to and checking with calculation.

blocks.h3: Three money tools of the year

blocks: **Two figures for the whole year.** The Wheel in the minus loses to someone who sees the situation in figures. Two are enough. The first is the free balance of the month: income minus obligatory expenses. The second is the reserve in months: how many months of living your savings will cover. Update them once a month, on a day chosen for this. When a chance comes, you see in a minute whether you can afford it.
**An offer to “decide today”.** The year promises such offers, and they should have a procedure:

ol: Say thank you and ask for the terms in writing.
Take a day, however much you are rushed.
Work out the worst case: how much you lose if it doesn’t work, and whether your reserve can withstand it.
Show the terms to someone who has no interest in the deal.
If the offer disappeared within a day, that was your answer.

blocks: **Checking a partner and a contract in the year of the Lovers.** The plus of the year is alliances, the hint of the year is Justice, so an alliance in 2027 is tested on paper. Before starting a joint venture, answer four questions in writing: who is responsible for what; what happens if one wants to leave; how money is shared, including losses; when you review the terms. Talk to someone who has already worked with this person. And start with a small joint undertaking for one or two months before taking on a big one.

blocks.h3: Three money scenarios of the year

blocks: Below are three scenarios that arise from the points of the year and your chart. These are hypotheses, not predictions: the year itself will show whether you recognise yourself in them.

**“Instinct without a cushion.”** You notice an opportunity before others — that is your main talent, the Wheel. The opportunity requires investing quickly, there is no reserve, and you invest your last money or borrow. If you were lucky, fine; if not, in a couple of months you are back at a familiar point, only with a new obligation. This is the minus of the Wheel in pure form: repetition. The way out is the two figures of the year and the procedure for “decide today” offers.

**“Sprint and slump.”** You earn in spurts, as the Chariot is used to: a month of working yourself into the ground, then fatigue. Fatigue is treated with purchases and comfort — in May the Empress stands in the minus, in October in the weak spot. By the end of the year what you earned and what you spent come out almost even, though there was a lot of work. The way out is an even pace, which is exactly the lesson of Strength.

**“An alliance of two independent people.”** You find a partner, client or co-author with whom each does their own thing: the Lovers and the Hermit in the plus of the year. The terms are written down from the very start, as the hint of the year demands. Such an alliance grows slowly and steadily and by autumn, when the Lovers become the result of the year, may become the main money result of 2027. The scenario has one risk — agreeing verbally and sorting out the details later.

blocks.h3: Work and business

blocks: If you are employed, the year supports a conversation about your area of responsibility and authority (Strength, the Emperor), about new pay terms (May) and about a freer work format (the Hermit, the World). If you have your own business, the year is good for partnerships, contracts and entering new markets and poorly suited for “all on one” bets. In 2027 a steadily growing income is worth more than one lucky month.
actions: Set up the two figures of the year — the free balance of the month and the reserve in months — and update them once a month.
Put every “decide today” offer through the five steps of the procedure.
Before an alliance or a contract, answer four questions in writing: roles, exit, money, review date.
Start a partnership with a small joint undertaking for one or two months.

chapters.h2: The plan for 2027 and the transition to 2028
chapters.conclusion: The first third is inventory, pause, start and check; the second is deals, rebuilding, mentoring and rest; the third is a change in money, harvest, choice and settling accounts. The Strength you master in 2027 will become a support and at the same time a material test in 2028, and the centre of 2028 will be taken by Justice.

cards.label: Centre of 2028
cards.caption: Justice — the main background of the next year. The same energy is the hint of 2027, the main point of your material karma and the decade from 40 to 50.

timeline.title: Year of the Chariot
timeline.text: The centre of the year’s matrix matched your main energy: speed and drive worked for you.

timeline.title: Year of Strength
timeline.text: A new energy in the centre: endurance, an even pace, leadership without pressure. The Wheel in both minuses: a chance for the prepared.

timeline.title: Year of Justice
timeline.text: The centre is honest calculation and making things official. The Strength of 2027 moves into the support and the material point, the Chariot into the plus. The year you turn forty.

blocks.h3: January–April: sort through and rebuild

ul: **Start:** an inventory of obligations and money (January), one rebuilding by plan, a conversation in the family, launching the main undertaking of the year (March).
**Finish:** what has outlived itself — before starting the new (February); old money habits you will notice at the April check.
**Don’t:** make decisions in anger, demolish without a plan, return to the past just because it called.

blocks.h3: May–August: consolidate and sustain

ul: **Start:** the decision put off since winter (May), sales and a new price (May), rebuilding at home or at work (June), mentoring and a family get-together (July), a holiday (August).
**Finish:** distributing roles in the main undertaking — by August it should hold without your daily push.
**Don’t:** fight for status, work without days off, make big purchases outside the budget.

blocks.h3: September–December: choose and close

ul: **Start:** one change in money (September), a conversation about a new place or terms (September), negotiations on alliances, a plan for 2028 (December).
**Finish:** the January inventory — with a check in October; projects at ninety per cent (November); debts, signatures and promises (December).
**Don’t:** choose under pressure, especially in November; spend “as a reward to yourself” beyond the budget; lecture people at the festive table.

blocks.h3: Checkpoints of the year

blocks: It is handy to keep the year as a calendar: a few dates on which you stop for fifteen minutes and check yourself. Each is taken from the chapter of its month or third.

What to check

blocks.h3: How to tell which side of the year you are on

blocks: Each energy of the year has a plus and a minus, and during the year it is useful to check from time to time which side is closer right now. This is not a test with right answers. If on some point you recognise yourself in the right-hand column, it is simply a hint about where to direct your attention in the coming month.

selfcheck.label: Strength — the centre of the year
plus: There is a lot to do, yet sleep and rest stay on schedule
In an argument you state your position once and hold the pause
The load grows gradually, without spurts and crashes
minus: You work without days off “for the sake of a sprint” and get angry with those who can’t keep up
Having the last word in an argument matters more than the decision
You keep control of what you could delegate
A week of pushing is followed by a week of emptiness

selfcheck.label: The Wheel — money and trials of the year
plus: The two figures of the year are at hand, and you accept a chance calmly
Recognising a familiar scenario, you take a step differently
“Decide today” offers go through the procedure from the chapter on money
minus: Returning to schemes and people who have let you down before
Failures are explained by bad luck

selfcheck.label: The Lovers — the plus of the year
plus: You choose and formalise your choice
Allies have appeared in your work and your life
Agreements are written down and clear to both sides
minus: An eternal “we’ll see” on important questions
Choices are made under pressure or out of pity

selfcheck.label: The Hermit — the support of the year
plus: There are hours that belong only to you
The main undertaking gets the best time of the day
You know how to say “no” to what is unnecessary
minus: After a heavy load you vanish from everyone

selfcheck.label: The Tower — the weak spot of the year
plus: What has outlived itself is closed calmly and completely

You promise exactly what you can deliver
New places and people expand your affairs

blocks.h3: The first step

blocks: The first step can be taken on the day you decide to live 2027 by this plan — whether before January or in the middle of the year. Take a sheet of paper and write three lines. The first is one undertaking you will run at an even pace, without spurts. The second is one rule for arguments: for example, “I come back to a difficult conversation only when I’ve cooled down.” The third is the money question of the year from the key chapter: am I preparing a chance or waiting for luck. These three lines are Strength, the tail and the Wheel translated into the language of an ordinary week. Put the sheet where you will see it.

blocks.h3: How 2027 turns into 2028

blocks: The 2028 matrix shows that the skill of 2027 doesn’t disappear. Strength, the centre of this year, stands in two points at once in 2028: in the upper left corner, the support of the next year, and in the right one, the material point. The endurance you build up now will become something to lean on and the thing that tests how you handle money. If in 2027 you learn to keep a pace, in 2028 it will be your resource. If not, the lesson will repeat, but this time in the material point.

The Chariot, your main energy, stands in the upper point in 2028, in the pure plus: after a year of endurance, speed works for you again, but now under control. The centre of 2028 is 8, Justice, the hint of 2027 and your material task: in October 2028, when you turn forty, a decade under Justice begins. The left point of 2028 is 22, the Fool, which December 2027 tries out in advance. The upper right corner is 18, the Moon, your trigger: the weak spot of the next year is anxiety and fog. And the sum of all the points of 2028 is 5, the Hierophant, your centre.

The result is a consistent story. 2026 was the year of your speed. 2027 teaches you to hold it. 2028 tests how held speed works in honest calculation and opens a decade in which honest calculation will become the main thing. In this story 2027 is the most important year for skill: it gives a second tool without which the transition to forty will be harder.
actions: Write the three lines of the year on the day you decide to live it by this plan: an undertaking at an even pace, a rule for arguments, the money question.
Transfer the checkpoints of the year to your calendar with a reminder a day before.
In December 2027, reread this plan and mark what of it has become a habit — that is what you will take into 2028.

faq.q: What does Strength in the centre of the year mean for me and what do I do with it?
a: Strength in the centre is the way the year asks you to carry everything that falls on you. There will be a lot of work and responsibility: in Lisovskaya’s list Strength means “many projects”, leadership, organisation. The question is what you carry this load with. You have four Chariots, and your usual way is speed and drive. The year offers a second one: an even pace, a calm tone, a pause before answering.
What it looks like in practice:

ul: at work you spread a big project over weeks and keep the pace instead of storming it overnight;
at a meeting or in a family argument you hold a pause before answering and let the other finish;
you talk about what hurt you once you have cooled down — in the evening or the next day;
in sport and physical load you build up gradually: Strength loves recovery, its minus is burnout;
when leading people, you set the pace by those walking alongside you.

a: The check is simple: if by the end of the year you have done a lot without burning out either yourself or your relationships with people, Strength is mastered. If you have done a lot at the cost of constant conflict and fatigue, the year was lived on your usual Chariot. That is not a failure, but the lesson will return in 2028, where Strength stands both in the support and in the material point.

faq.q: The year is already under way — what can I still do?
a: The answer depends on when you opened this report. If there is time before January, write down the three lines of the year from the plan and start keeping the two money figures from the chapter on money: by January you will have a starting point.

If the year is already under way, find your third. January–April: inventory, close what has outlived itself, launch the main undertaking and break nothing in the heat of the moment. May–August: make the postponed decision, name a price, rebuild by plan, have a real rest. September–December: one change in money, a check in October, a slow choice in November, settling accounts in December. What you missed is not lost: January rhymes with October, February with November, March with December.

faq.q: The Wheel in both minuses — does that mean money will go badly?
a: No. A minus in the year’s matrix is a place of trials, not a verdict. Lisovskaya advises reading these points first as a minus, then as a plus. The minus of the Wheel is impulsive decisions, debts, trusting the wrong person, repeating old schemes. The plus is opportunities, luck, a big payout, debts being repaid. Which side comes to the fore depends largely on whether you are ready for the moment.

For you the Wheel is your main talent, a sense of the moment, and the year tests this talent with calculation. The tools for this — the two figures of the year and the procedure for “decide today” offers — are gathered in the chapter on money.

faq.q: The Tower in the weak spot and on the ring — should I expect destruction?
a: The Tower in the weak spot of the year is not a prediction of disaster. According to the book this point shows weaknesses in front of others: what to postpone, what throws you off. The Tower’s weakness is tearing everything down at once when something doesn’t suit you: slamming the door, leaving in the heat of the moment, saying something harsh. Lisovskaya classes the Tower as an energy of change and writes directly that such changes are “not necessarily negative”.

Until April the Tower also stands on the age ring, so in the first months of the year it is especially worth guarding against decisions made in anger. But rebuilding according to a plan is possible and necessary: in June the Tower rises into the plus of the month, and that is the best time for renovation — at home, at work, in your habits.

faq.q: Which months are better for decisions and contracts, and which for a pause?

ul: **For starting and moving:** March and December — the Chariot in the centre and in the support.

**For choice, deals and money:** May (the Lovers in the centre, your talent and profit points in the plus), September (changes in money, the Sun and the Wheel in the plus), October (harvest, Judgement in the plus).
**For a pause and review:** February and November — the Hanged Man in the centre; August — the Hermit in the centre.
**For a check:** April — a scaled-down copy of the year.
**For rebuilding:** June — the Tower in the plus.
**For mentoring and family:** July — your centre matches the centre of the month.

a: The hardest month for an important choice is November, when the Lovers stand in the minus. If a decision ripens in autumn, it is better to make it in September–October or let it rest until December.

faq.q: The Lovers from April — is that a promise of new love?
a: The matrix makes no promises. The Lovers on the age ring from April, in the plus of the year and in the result of the last third say that the theme of choice and alliance comes to the fore in these months. For a person in a couple this may be a renewal of the relationship, a shared project, an agreement about a new life together. For someone single — more interest in meeting people and more readiness for it. For work — partnerships and contracts.
What you do with it is up to you. The matrix only suggests a condition: a choice made from a calm place holds better this year than a choice made under pressure.

faq.q: The Chariot is me. Do I now have to slow down all year?
a: No. The Chariot stays yours, and the year doesn’t ask you to become a different person. It asks you to add a second tool to speed. A useful rule for the whole year: act fast and decide slowly — about people and about money.

ul: **Where speed is supported:** March and December, when the Chariot stands in the centre and in the support of the month; September, with the Sun and the Wheel in the plus; launching undertakings and trips all year.

**Where speed costs dearly:** arguments and power struggles, especially in January, when the Emperor is in the minus; July, where the Chariot stands in the point of trials; May, where it is in the weak spot — at the peak of success you want to speed up even more.
**Where speed is better replaced with a pause:** February, November and August — the months of the Hanged Man and the Hermit.

a: In short: your speed is the engine, the year’s Strength is the steering wheel. In 2027 the winner is whoever has both.

faq.q: Can I change jobs, move or make big purchases in 2027?
a: The year’s matrix neither forbids nor prescribes anything: it shows where such steps have more support and where more risk.

ul: **Changing jobs.** The Emperor in the lower corner of the year supports promotion, a good position, a business of your own; Judgement supports searching for a new occupation. The most suitable months are May (contracts), September (Death in the centre: a new job, a project, a transfer; the Sun in the plus: changing jobs) and October (harvest).

**A move or a long trip.** The Emperor in a forecast includes planning a move and a long trip; the World in the left point means travel and moving. It is convenient to plan in the first half of the year, but the decision shouldn’t be made in anger while the Tower stands in the weak spot and on the ring until April.

**Big purchases.** June, when the Tower is in the plus, is good for housing, renovation and equipment; October for purchases out of what you have earned, as long as your birthday doesn’t turn into a financial hole. August is not the best time: the Hermit in the minus means financial restrictions. And all year — no purchases on an offer that is valid only today.

faq.q: I don’t have my own business, a team or clients. How do I apply this advice?
a: The report is written for any way of life, and its words can be translated into yours.

ul: **“The main undertaking of the year”** is any goal you pursue all year: a project at work, study, sport, a renovation, a move, a book, your family’s health.
**“An ally” and “a team”** mean at least one person who knows about your goal and helps: a colleague, a friend, a coach, someone close.
**“Name a price”** means a conversation about salary, about a new role, about extra work becoming paid or no longer being yours.
**“Mentoring”** means explaining to a newcomer what you know how to do, helping a child with studies, telling a friend how you solved a problem.
**“Partnership”** means any shared project with another person, from a trip together to a family budget.

a: The energies of the year work the same way in an office, at home and in your own business. Strength is endurance wherever a load falls on you; the Wheel is a chance you are ready for, whether a new position or a good purchase.

faq.q: How does this year prepare me for forty?
a: 2027 stands in the middle of the transition Lisovskaya describes as the change from the personal purpose to the social one, roughly from 37 to 43. Your personal purpose is 5, the Hierophant, and it matches your centre: before forty you unfold through knowledge, rules, the ability to teach. The social one is 10, the Wheel: the ability to see the course of events and work with change. The Wheel stands in both minuses of the 2027 matrix, and the year lets you try this role in difficult conditions.

Besides, the hint of the year, Justice, will open the decade from 40 to 50 and stand in the centre of 2028. From October 2027 the last year of the decade of the Moon begins: a good time to close what has dragged on since your early thirties and approach forty with clear calculation.

chakras.title: Chakras: the energy map, reading the seven levels for matrix 7–10–8
chakras.lead: It begins with what gives you a sense of home. Then come desire, action, relationships, words and understanding. Last comes meaning — the reason you want to keep going. This is a symbolic portrait drawn from your matrix: seven chakras, each showing a different side of one life.

chakraRows.title: Muladhara
chakraRows.heading: Solid ground made of what you've earned
paragraphs: The figures in your account aren't an abstraction for you — they feel like solid ground. Daily life is run along the lines of Justice: spending is recorded, obligations are met on time, and everything you have was honestly come by. The Chariot fuels the wish to save, to expand, to move towards a tangible goal and, after any setback, to pull yourself together and make up lost ground. The Devil shows what your sense of security rests on. It is firmly tied to the material: to the amount, to possessions, to the standard of living you've secured for yourself.

**Security, for you, is what has been earned, accounted for and belongs to you.** Imagine you are saving for a home of your own. You have a spreadsheet, a plan and a clear timeline, and every stage you complete feels like a small victory. Here your attachment to the result works as fuel: it helps you turn down impulse purchases and stay on course when things get dull. The goal comes closer every month, and you can see it in the numbers.

But attachment has a way of turning into a chain. The safety cushion must keep growing, and any deviation — a broken appliance, a rent rise — feels like a threat rather than an ordinary expense. Holidays are put off; rest feels like a luxury you haven't earned yet. The Devil's hold is not for ever, and the chain can be taken off. But first you have to notice: the sum has long been enough, and the calm still hasn't come.

chakraRows.title: Svadhisthana
chakraRows.heading: Letting go, standing still, then setting off again
paragraphs: It matters to you that a favourite pastime stays a choice, not a chore. Death shows in how you spend your time: a club or hobby that has turned into an obligation is something you can walk away from without lengthy excuses. The Hanged Man explains where new desire comes from: it surfaces in a pause, when you have nothing to do and see your life from another side. The Chariot shapes what stays with you afterwards — the thrill of movement and the sense that you are holding the reins yourself again.

**Your fresh start is born of an honest pause.** Say you leave the choir where you had been singing out of habit, and for a month you simply go for walks in the evening. In that emptiness, one day it becomes clear what you really want: to put together a small band of your own and play the music you love. The decision came from within, so its energy is your own as well. Every step feels like a small victory.

The hardest part is the pause itself. Once something ends, the empty evenings make you uneasy, and you want to get racing again as soon as you can — sign up for something, set a new goal, fill the diary. You skip over the pause, and the next thing gets chosen on the move, on the first pretext that comes along. The thrill of the first weeks is there, but six months later the new pastime weighs on you just as the old one did. The scenery changes, but the circle repeats: the outside view that made it worth standing still never had time to appear.

chakraRows.title: Manipura
chakraRows.heading: A proven method amid the turns
paragraphs: Behind your independent work stands a school: a method you have mastered, the accepted rules of your profession, the experience of those who walked this path before you. You act through the Hierophant’s recognised order — first find out how things are done, then do them just as well and pass the skill on to others. But the same Hierophant also answers the question of where your strength comes from: from the certainty that you are doing the right thing and standing on solid ground. You experience the result through the image of the Wheel of Fortune — good and bad luck feel like the turning of a wheel, where ups and downs follow one another.

A proven method becomes your axis when circumstances start to spin. A job falls through, the terms change, plans shift — you still have what you do well, and you can come back to it tomorrow. **A downturn does not cancel out mastery, and luck does not replace it.** This attitude lets you get through a bad patch calmly and keep your head on the way up.

Trouble begins when you expect doing things right to secure the outcome. The wheel turns against you, and you do the same thing even more carefully, even more strictly by the rules. It happens again, and you begin to feel that you did everything right and the rest is up to luck. Between rule and fate, the room for your own decision quietly vanishes: what to change yourself, now that the old way has stopped working.

chakraRows.title: Anahata
chakraRows.heading: Yours through every twist and turn
paragraphs: Someone close to you remains yours come what may — in good luck and in failure. Judgement explains the motive: a need for a deep bond, for the sense that you belong to each other regardless of circumstance. The Star turns that bond into action — after a setback, you are the first to bring hope and help. And the Wheel of Fortune in your feelings is a sharp sense of life’s turns: change brings you alive, but at times it pulls the ground from under your feet.

**No twist of fate changes the fact that your loved one is yours.** Say their business has gone under. You don’t let them drown in the failure: you help with their CV, remind them what they are good at, keep the usual rhythm at home. They know their place beside you doesn’t depend on a job title, and within a month they can already see this turn as a beginning rather than an end.

A loved one’s setback is easy to mistake for a sign that only you can see. The business has closed, and to you it’s obvious: it’s time to take up what they dreamed of when they were young. You light up, find courses, sketch out a budget. But for now they just want to find a similar job and catch their breath. Your excitement next to their bewilderment sounds like a reproach, as if they can’t hear their own destiny. A call that a person has to answer for themselves reaches them in your voice — and they no longer feel like answering.

cells.caption: A keen sense of turning points

chakraRows.title: Vishuddha
chakraRows.heading: Hearing others out and naming your interest
paragraphs: When a lot hangs on a conversation, you may be in no hurry to speak. The Hanged Man gives your speech a pause: first hear the other person out, look at the question through their eyes, ask again. Behind this unhurried manner lies a strong desire. The Devil shows how tightly the outcome you need can hold on to you until the decision you hope for has been spoken. The Hermit takes your response inwards: you mull over other people’s words on your own, and your reaction takes time to ripen.

**A strong wish to influence things can make you a very attentive listener.** Say you want to keep a friend involved in a project you share. Instead of persuading them, you ask what is weighing on them and hear the main thing: it is not tiredness but the fact that nobody notices their ideas. After some thought you have one precise proposal ready, and an honest “It matters to me that you stay.” Your interest has been said out loud, and the other person feels heard.

Something once confided in you can become a point in an argument. The agreement you wanted did not come, your frustration sank deep, and alone you go back over everything you heard before. Later the most precise piece comes into play: “You said yourself you were afraid you couldn’t cope.” That is hard to answer, and you may well win the argument. But the other person remembers that their openness was turned into a case against them. They begin to tell you less, and your best skill — listening — loses its ground.

chakraRows.title: Ajna
chakraRows.heading: Plain clarity and an honest result
paragraphs: It is easier for you to understand when everything is out in the open. Your way of thinking comes from the Sun: no hazy hints, plain words, a picture you could show to someone else. The Chariot turns a question into a road with a destination, and the thrill grows with every step towards the answer. And you weigh the outcome on the scales of Justice: a conclusion satisfies you when it is honestly balanced by the facts, and it is easier to admit your own mistake than to leave the account crooked.

Your family is choosing between two mortgage offers, and the discussion has been going round in circles for a week. You sit down with a spreadsheet: rates, total cost, early repayment terms — all in one row, all in view. Within an hour there is an answer, and everyone understands it, not just you. **You can turn a tangled question into a clear decision that stands up to scrutiny.** If you found a slip of your own along the way, you say so out loud: an honest result matters more than being right.

Questions without a clear answer are harder. The Chariot needs to arrive, Justice needs to close the account, and uncertainty feels almost like unfairness: the scales hang in the air while everything stalls. Then you are tempted to deliver a verdict before there are enough facts, and to call obvious what is simply convenient to see in daylight. Other people’s doubts start to look like stubbornness, and the discussion like a trial. A decision is made, but whatever didn’t fit in the spreadsheet hasn’t gone anywhere.

chakraRows.title: Sahasrara
chakraRows.heading: Holding your course as life turns
paragraphs: The meaning of your path is tested at the turns — where circumstances change but you want to keep your direction. The Chariot works through your actions: you choose a goal, overcome obstacles and steer things where you have decided they should go. The Wheel of Fortune gives you footing: life moves in cycles, highs give way to lows, and there is an order of its own in that change. The Star brings hope to the journey — it returns even after a stage that went badly, and you want to share it.

**For you, a change is not the end of the road but a new stretch of it.** Say a plan you have put a lot into falls through for reasons beyond your control. After the first flash of annoyance, you ask not “Why me?” but “Where to now?” The direction stays and the route changes: you take what the turn has opened up and pick up speed again. Perhaps the people travelling beside you also begin to see a setback as a bend in the road rather than its end.

Hope can fuse so firmly with your course that every turn starts to confirm it. Good luck is a sign you are on the right track; bad luck is a test before the breakthrough. The Chariot drives you on, and reasons to keep going can always be found. But then change stops telling you anything: a downturn that might have pointed to another direction has been explained in advance. Your inspiration rests on how you read events rather than on the events themselves, even though life may have offered you a different turning more than once.

energyField.title: Overall energy field
energyField.topic: The shared tone of all seven levels
energyField.heading: Quietly letting go of what is over
paragraphs: Your life divides neatly into chapters, and you live each one in earnest. You go your own way, unhurried and thoughtful, relying more on your own experience than on other people’s advice — that is the Hermit. Death appears twice. In how your strength is spread, it means your energy is freed when something has come to an end: a stage, a role, a familiar way of life. In your emotions it is responsible for something else — the ability to truly say goodbye, to live an ending through rather than pretend it never happened.

**You know how to let go — and come out of a change as a different person.** You live through loss or disappointment without putting it on show: you withdraw into yourself, go over what happened and let the old pain run its course. But afterwards you come back with a clarity you did not have before. That is why people are drawn to you at times of transition: you know how to get through an ending without getting stuck in it, and you can show that road to others.

The other side is final decisions made too quietly. Inside, the door has already closed, but outwardly nothing has changed: you go on talking politely, going to the same job, answering messages. The person next to you does not suspect that for you this chapter has been read to the end, and they are the last to find out. They never had a second chance, because there was never a conversation. The goodbye took place entirely in your head.

karmic_tail.title: Karmic tail
paragraphs: Two of the three cards in the 12-19-7 tail speak the language of war in the sources; the third is a man hung upside down. Popular readings call it the “Warrior” after a legend: in a past life the soul was supposedly a warrior whose strength brought others death and destruction, and who died suddenly, “not according to plan”. This cannot be checked. But as a metaphor it is accurate: this is life on a **war footing**. There is always a front, an enemy and a righteous cause. Peacetime does not calm; it alarms.

The name rests on more than legend. Waite’s divinatory list for the Chariot reads “war, triumph, presumption, vengeance”. For Wen, the Chariot speaks of “military prowess” and the Sun signifies “a warrior king and chieftain”. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the matrix, so this proves nothing. But the coincidence is telling.

The third card breaks ranks. The Hanged Man accounts for the darkest part of the legend — a life broken off mid-sentence. Waite sees in him “life in suspension, but life and not death”. Wen adds a detail that seems written for this tail: the hanged man’s hands are hidden because “his ultimate offering to the world has yet to be seen”. Hence the feeling “I could have, but…”: the real work waits until some war is over.

paragraphs.h3: Here the brightest card in the deck keeps the books

paragraphs: The circle starts with a noble move: the cause first, me later. Wen on the Hanged Man: “There is a greater good at stake and it is the Seeker who will make the sacrifice.” Personal life waits for victory: the holiday after the deadline, relationships after the promotion, rest once things settle down.

The sacrifice has to pay off, and the Sun pays for it. Wen describes it as success that brings “recognition, applause, or accolades”, and a red banner “that calls attention to the Seeker”. **Light is credited for every battle won.** So this tail is bad at losing: defeat is not a setback but the devaluing of everything given.

After victory comes peacetime, and it frightens. An engineer called in whenever things are on fire rescues three projects everyone had written off, at the cost of his nights and two holidays. He is thanked at an all-hands and is happy for a couple of weeks. Then a calm quarter arrives and everything grates: people “can’t keep up”. A month later he finds a new fire — or starts one himself. The Sun of this tail is switched on by victory, and victory exists only in war.

After defeat the circle closes differently: the person gets stuck. Outside, “I don’t want anything”; inside, anger with nowhere to go. Often the two loops alternate: years of patient service, an outburst of “enough, now we do it my way”, a run of victories, burnout and back to hanging. Waite seems to warn those stuck in endurance: the Hanged Man “has been called falsely a card of martyrdom… a card of duty”.

paragraphs.h3: The charioteer can win but cannot bless himself

paragraphs: The root holds the lesson, and it is not courage — of that there is plenty. Waite calls the charioteer “above all things triumph in the mind”, but the planes of his conquest are “manifest or external and not within himself”. Wen asks who exactly is in control, the sphinxes or the charioteer. A person with 12-19-7 can win battles for years without once choosing the course: the next war sets it.

A hidden fourth card shows who declares that war. Everyone with 12-19-7 has 5, the Hierophant, in the centre of the matrix, and the tail’s formulas read almost like a sentence. The Hanged Man = the Chariot + the Hierophant: a warrior plus a rulebook gives sacrifice. The Sun = the Chariot + the Hanged Man: a warrior plus sacrifice gives glory.

In Waite the Hierophant is “the order and the head of the recognized hierarchy”, and his divinatory list runs “marriage, alliance, captivity, servitude” — almost the full vocabulary of a soldier’s fate. Of the charioteer Waite says pointedly: “He is not hereditary royalty and he is not priesthood.” **The charioteer can win, but he cannot bless himself.** Yet everyone with this tail has a priest in the centre of the chart. Out of habit the Warrior hands the right to decide which war is righteous to someone else — a company, a family, a party, an idea. In our interpretation, this is why popular readings of 12-19-7 so often mention feuds with former allies: one day the order turns out to be people protecting themselves first.

paragraphs.h3: The real question is not “fight or give up?” but “whose war is this?”

paragraphs: Institutions need not be abandoned: a warrior without a rulebook is a mercenary. The key is for the Hierophant to move inside — to serve the cause, not the department, and to notice when “the righteous cause” becomes somebody’s interest. Then victory needs no blessing from outside. The author’s exercises — not a ritual, not a promise of results:

ul: List every current fight and mark it “mine”, “inherited” or “someone else’s, but I’m the one fighting”.
Peace terms before the fight: what counts as victory, and where to stop even without winning. Then the Hanged Man’s pause becomes a halt rather than a defeat.
Write down five to seven personal rules that hold even if a company or a family scraps them.
When the urge to punish comes, wait a day before striking back. As Wen puts it: “It is not for the Seeker to administer judgment, vengeance, or penance.”

paragraphs: In a couple the script is the same: everyone with 12-19-7 also has the Hanged Man at the start of the relationship line. Love begins with service that expects a medal, and the partner becomes a commander or a “safe home front” — a phrase with the army already in it. Win the argument, lose the evening. The Chariot person, according to Wen, “deep down is quite vulnerable and sensitive”: armour is worn by those who hurt too much. The bravest thing the Warrior can say in a couple is “I’m scared”, instead of attacking.
Where real war, military service or violence lies in the past, the tail has nothing to do with it, and its metaphors are no substitute for professional help.

paragraphs.h3: A warrior who needs no enemy

paragraphs: In the lived-through version the person gives themselves to a great cause, carries it to victory and keeps hold of the reins. They get called in a crisis and are the first to defend the weak. A rulebook they wrote themselves turns them into **someone who cannot be bought and cannot be made to fight someone else’s war**.

Waite’s charioteer is “an erect and princely figure carrying a drawn sword”. His child of the Sun is also a rider and a victor with a red banner, but rides a white horse with neither armour nor clothes. The light of this card is direct, not reflected: reflected light needs an audience, direct light shines by itself. Waite links the card with coming out “from the walled garden of the sensitive life” and “passing on the journey home”. This is what 12-19-7 lived through looks like: **a victory that needs no armour, and the road home after the war**.
